html:
The Nuu-chah-nulth, once called Nootka, are a group of related First Nations on the west coast of Vancouver Island, British Columbia. Their name means "all along the mountains and sea", and their Wakashan language is related to those of the Kwakwaka'wakw and the Makah.

They were among the few peoples of the coast who hunted whales, from big cedar canoes, and they fished, gathered and held feasts such as the potlatch.

  • In 1778 James Cook spent a month at Nootka Sound, and the sale of the sea otter furs his crew got there in China started the maritime fur trade.
  • Their chief Maquinna at Yuquot dealt with British and Spanish traders, and Spain built a fort there in 1789.
  • The quarrel over that fort, the Nootka Crisis of 1789 to 1790, nearly led to war between Britain and Spain.

Today they include nations such as the Tseshaht, Hupacasath and Huu-ay-aht, and the Maa-nulth treaty of 2011 gave five of them self-government.
